extracted.intended_audience: Indian agents, Bureau of Indian Affairs officials, and Interior Department policymakers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and policy criteria for administration of Indian agencies, reservations, schools, police, medical care, supplies, and self-support programs as reflected in an 1880 annual report index.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patents for allotted lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents for lands, granting of, to Indians of Puyallup Agency urged; to allottees of land urged; to lands allotted at LaPointe Agency not received, source of great trouble to agent; want of title, source of anxiety to S'Kokomish Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting patents to allottees is recommended to secure titles, prevent disputes, and remove sources of administrative trouble where lack of patents causes anxiety and operational problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and reliability of Indian police
rubrics_metrics.description: Indian police — all reports from agents bear uniform testimony to value, reliability, and fidelity of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess Indian police by their demonstrated reliability in preserving order, protecting agency property, and assisting during issues (e.g., rations); note examples of highly commended forces and agencies with none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate pay for Indian police
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief obstacle in perfecting system inadequate pay of; force impossible to organize among Navajoes on account of small pay allowed; increase of pay urged; Congress should allow department discretionary power as to salaries of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient and discretionary salary levels to recruit and retain police, recognizing inadequate pay prevents organization and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform and status parity for Indian police
rubrics_metrics.description: Police agent Rosebud Agency urges same pay and uniform as for regular United States soldiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equalizing uniform and pay with soldiers is recommended to raise status, pride, and effectiveness of Indian police and improve recruitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and composition of police forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Best men should belong to [the force]; on consolidated White Earth Reserve highly commended; Indians sometimes refuse to serve for pay allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select trustworthy, well-regarded men for police duties; composition and willingness to serve affect force efficiency and community acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties and importance of Indian police
rubrics_metrics.description: Duties of [police] varied; important benefits resulting from establishment of; preserve order and render assistance during rations issues; protect public agency buildings; attend to arrests and discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate police by scope of duties and outcomes: maintaining public order, protecting property, assisting in administration (rations), and enforcing agency discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of physicians to agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Physician, appointment of, urged for Lemhi Agency; none at Shoshone and Bannock Agency, and much needed; question of return of physician to Malheur from Yakama should be definitely settled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign physicians where sanitary indicators or physician reports show need; lack of physicians is a policy gap to be remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitary condition metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanitary condition of Indians reported by births and deaths (e.g., '62 births and 49 deaths'); disease prevalence (scrofulous diseases, malaria, syphilis) and hospital facilities considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use birth/death statistics, disease incidence, and availability of hospital accommodations as metrics to evaluate public health needs and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of boarding and industrial schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Boarding and industrial schools: success of day-school and manual labor; boarding schools recommended (e.g., to accommodate 200 pupils); industrial training lauded at many agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and support boarding/industrial schools emphasizing manual labor and industrial training, modeled on successful examples, to advance education and vocational skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of day schools and attendance incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Day schools are 'stepping-stones' to boarding/industrial schools; mid-day lunch cited as incentive to Indian children to attend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use day schools to transition children into longer-term training programs and employ attendance incentives (meals) to increase enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of school funding and treaty funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriations insufficient to meet increasing demands of Indians for schools; '50,000 Indians at 17 agencies have no treaty school funds whatever'; inadequacy of treaty funds emphasized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and augment appropriations and treaty school funds to match demand and equitable service provision across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: School cost and cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost per capita per annum for instruction in schools is $60, exclusive of rations; some boarding schools unremunerative for the expense incurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure per-capita instructional cost and compare outcomes; consider cost-effectiveness when deciding program continuation or expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surveying and establishing reservation boundaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey of Devils Lake Reservation urged to settle disputed claims; re-run lines of Nez Perce Agency needed to prevent trouble; '6,000 miles of boundaries remain unsurveyed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and re-check surveys and boundary lines promptly to prevent trespass, squatter conflicts, and legal disputes; prioritize unsettled reservation boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies procurement, timeliness, and storage
rubrics_metrics.description: Long delay in receiving supplies after purchase and shipment is source of annoyance; storehouse crowded at some agencies; 'saving of $11,000 at Pine Ridge in exercising judgment in issues.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure timely procurement, adequate storage facilities, and prudent issue practices to reduce waste, delays, and achieve cost savings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ration issuance policy and targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Rations issues varied: 'all except beef stopped July 1, 1879, at request of Indians of Osage Agency'; 'issued only to Pi-Utes, police, and apprentices at Warm Springs Agency'; 'none issued to any tribes on Sac and Fox Reserve, Indian Territory, except partially to Mexican Kickapoos.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design ration policies tailored to local conditions and groups (e.g., police, apprentices), and adjust issues to reduce dependence while meeting actual needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote self-support via farming, stock-raising, and fisheries
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-supporting tribes listed; fisheries chief sources at Pyramid Lake and Walker River; many tribes cultivate acreage and own large herds; examples of near self-support among various agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote agriculture, stock-raising, and fisheries through training, provision of implements and stock, and suitable land use to reduce dependence on federal aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and support of livestock and implements
rubrics_metrics.description: Live and farming implements distributed to working Indians of Standing Rock Agency; recommendation that '500 head should be purchased yearly for Tanktons' for two or three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide livestock and implements as starter capital and sustain periodic purchases to build productive herds and enable agricultural self-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequacy of Indian agent salaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Salaries of Indian agents totally inadequate, and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure agent salaries are sufficient to attract qualified administrators, since inadequate compensation undermines effective agency management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and oversight of renters/leases on reserves
rubrics_metrics.description: Renters on Quapaw Reserve — advantages to Indians from; 'abuses of privileges can be controlled by agent.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require active agent oversight of leasing/renting arrangements to prevent abuses and ensure renters benefit tribal interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt proven training-school models
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to Hampton or Carlisle as 'first in order of merit'; Carlisle training-school system described for conducting industrial education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use recognized successful models (Hampton/Carlisle) when designing and operating training and industrial schools; evaluate local schools against these benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annunity/cash payment policy effects on progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Large cash annuity obstacle to progress among Sac and Fox of Missouri at Great Nemaha Agency; annuity matters affect advancement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design annuity and payment mechanisms to avoid creating disincentives to productive labor and self-support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal and relocation as policy tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of certain bands recommended (e.g., Mescalero to Hot Springs Reservation; removal of Piute prisoners from Vancouver Barracks to Warm Springs Agency); removals urged for relief/support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use removals/relocations when supported by reasons of subsistence, security, or administrative efficiency, but evaluate impacts carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Police system's social benefits (reducing illicit influence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Police system curtailed influence of 'squaw-men' — 'infinite source of evil'; renegade Indians along Columbia River controlled; police reduce social ills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize broader social benefits of a functioning police force in reducing exploitative influences and controlling roaming or renegade elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and coordinate religious/missionary work
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominations assigned to agencies; religious societies contributed $8,810 past year for New York Indians; teachings among Western Shoshones conflued to one creed—the Golden Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate missionary and religious efforts as part of social/educational programs; track denominational assignments and contributions as adjuncts to agency work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide communication infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Telegraph line connecting Pine Ridge and Spotted Tail Agencies will soon be in operation; telegraph office established at Kiowa Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in communication infrastructure (telegraph, offices) to improve interagency coordination, responsiveness, and administration.
